summary.text: Michael Bahry is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate in Rhode Island. A Rhode Island native, he worked as a laborer, carpenter and construction executive and founded a Providence nonprofit before returning to school for two master's degrees in theology and biblical studies. He is running on ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars and on congressional term limits.

paragraphs.text: Bahry describes himself on his campaign website as a native Rhode Islander who has been married for more than 40 years and has two children and four grandchildren.
His career spanned work as a laborer, carpenter, construction executive and business owner, including running a commercial construction company.
According to the campaign, he earned a bachelor's degree from Providence College.
In 2014 he founded the nonprofit Fifty-Three: Five, which provides food, fellowship and support to families and the homeless in Providence, and he speaks monthly at the Providence Rescue Mission.
At age 53, Bahry returned to college and earned a Master of Theological Studies (2017) and a Master of Arts in Biblical Studies (2022) from Providence College.
He teaches theology at Salve Regina University, where local news described him as a visiting lecturer of three years, and he is the author of the book Hell Is a Bad Word.
He is a lector and finance committee member at Our Lady of Loreto Church, and he lives in East Providence.
Bahry announced in June 2026 a drive to gather the 1,000 signatures needed to appear on the ballot as an independent against Democratic Sen. Jack Reed.
